mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings growth and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250,000 new jobs per month for two consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 250000 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant for four consecutive months after a prior tightening cycle, it signals policy pause, allowing equity valuations to reprice based on improved earnings expectations, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for four consecutive months after at least two prior rate hikes
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not positive in at least 55% of triggered policy pause episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a sharp near-term demand shock, which reduces earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.6% for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.6% for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes with CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%.
